messages:
emily: quick q — if I need to flip the inference service kill-switch, who exactly is allowed to do that right now? names + preferred comms channel please. trying to avoid accidental flips during oncall.

chris: only SRE leads and Platform oncall can run the manual disable. names: @chris, @sre-oncall, @ops-manager. comms: post in #incident-ops and tag @oncall-lead. :thumbsup:

priya: confirm: does that include emergency overrides from security? last week sec asked to flip for suspected data leak.

security-ops: we can request a toggle but we don't have direct toggle perms. escalate to eng-sre lead or exec if needed. preferred flow: open a PagerDuty incident AND post a short summary in #incident-ops so the oncall can act.

emily: what's the exact command/path? I want to copy it into the runbook (so steps are unambiguous).

chris: command we use currently:
```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/flags/toggle" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \\
  -d '{"flag":"inference_v2_kill_switch","action":"disable","scope":"global","reason":"<short reason>"}'
```
note: must include an "audit_user" header if you're acting on someone else's behalf (service account proxy).

deploy-bot: Flag toggle recorded: inference_v2_kill_switch disabled by chris at 2024-11-02T14:12:31Z — audit-id: a1b2c3d4

sre-oncall: ops note: prefer scoped disables during canary windows — e.g. use "scope":"region:us-east-1" or "audience:canary-5%". global disables require SRE lead + 2FA confirmation.

priya: can we add a guardrail so global flips require two-person approval? also where is the audit trail stored exactly?

chris: audit logs land in the flags-audit ELK index (flags-audit-*). Kibana: https://kibana.redwood/flags-audit . each entry has audit-id, user, method, request-body, and timing. retention is 90d for prod. we also mirror audit events to the compliance S3 bucket for 1y.

emily: perfect. I'll update the runbook with names, comms, and the 2-person approval for global toggles. anyone object to adding "security-ops must be notified for any data-impacting flips"?

security-ops: no objection. please include an example notification template.

emily: draft template to include in runbook:
"URGENT: disabling inference_v2_kill_switch in us-east-1 for suspected data exposure. Actioned by @chris. audit-id: <audit-id>. Reason: <short reason>. PagerDuty incident: <link>."

chris: LGTM. add rollback steps: re-enable via the same endpoint with "action":"enable" and then run a post-action verification:
```
curl https://inference.redwood/healthz
# check recent request logs for 30s
```

sre-oncall: also add a requirement to open a follow-up postmortem within 72 hours when the kill-switch is used.

emily: thanks — I'll open a PR to the runbook, ping this thread when it's live, and tag you for review. :raised_hands:
